mn75:5.3: Bhūnahu—wreaker of being: whatever may be the etymology of this word, what it refers to here is shown by Māgaṇḍiya himself at 10.9-10.10 below. See para. 10, also; brahmins made much of having sons, while the Buddha led a celibate life after his renunciation, therefore Māgaṇḍiya accuses him as a ‘wreaker of being’.
mn75:9.2: That is, should he be called a ‘wreaker of being’ who is characterized by a negative attitude to the senses, or a wise man?
mn75:16.2: Remember that this includes both desires in oneself and pleasurable sense objects exterior to oneself.
mn75:20.6: Telamasikatena sāhuḷicīrena—grimy, oil-stained garment: tela-masikata is not commented on.
